modelingNotes: Manufacturer spelling LAD4RCU; source LAD-4RCU retained exactly. Matching RC technology, host ranges and mounting support treating the hyphen as a presentation separator.

Two-ended passive series RC network. LAD4RC installation illustration: https://download.se.com/files?p_Doc_Ref=1378322_01A55&p_File_Name=1378322_01A55-10.pdf&p_enDocType=Instruction+sheet , page 1, W9 1378322 0211 A10, 04/2021.
RC.1 and RC.2 are unordered functional authoring aliases for the two plug-in RC endpoints. They are not printed terminal numbers, polarity, top/bottom positions or a physical A1/A2 mating map.

Clipping establishes connection across the separately ordered host coil. The type does not import host contacts or coil terminals and does not create cross-device continuity. The RC network is not a fixed link or short circuit.
Legacy 250 V suitability is not established. No scalar nominal voltage is assigned.

For virtually sinusoidal voltage with less than 5% THD: peak limited to 3 Uc; oscillation at most 400 Hz; dropout 1.2–2 times normal. Natural RC frequency 100 Hz in B8/69's 110/240 V category is not mains frequency. No R/C values or current limit asserted.

Both functional attachment ends are required for an installed suppressor to operate. A physical clip-on connection must still be represented in project topology; no host mating map is automatically inferred. Host bonding is outside this accessory scope.
Generic load symbol represents the complete RC impedance. No dedicated RC circuit mark exists in the supplied symbol enum; internal junction and component geometry are not invented.

connectionCoverage.notes: Both functional plug-in endpoints in the LAD4RC diagram are represented. Physical contact markings and exact mating-position mapping remain undocumented; aliases assert neither. No additional power, PE, shield or communications connection is established. Host terminals and bonding are outside scope.
